title: SOURCE_TARGETS screen: TiFlash MPP logical core cache StartTimestamp token

evidence.interpretation: splitTiFlashLogicalCoreCache refreshes hardware info only when cached StartTimestamp differs from InfoSchema server info
TiFlash store info exposes seconds-level StartTimestamp
MPPServerInfoManager caches LogicalCPUCount by address with StartTimestamp as freshness token

gate_assessment.G1_token_gated_decision: pass: equal StartTimestamp gates cache reuse vs hardware-info refresh
gate_assessment.G2_lifecycle_overlap: pass: cached MPPServerInfo can outlive a TiFlash lifecycle change at the same address
gate_assessment.G3_product_feasible_collision_schedule: not_proven: the red schedule requires TiFlash restart/re-registration in the same second, address reuse, and changed logical CPU count; forcing equal StartTimestamp in a unit test would not prove product feasibility
gate_assessment.G4_strong_state_action_oracle: weak_pass: stale LogicalCPUCount can affect TiFlashFineGrainedShuffleStreamCount in the physical plan, but the consequence is planner/performance quality rather than row-set correctness or recovery safety

payload.retired_reason: The source shape matches identity-token async filtering, but the schedule and consequence are too weak for current bug-hunt priority. Keep as selector calibration instead of executing a low-quality forced-token RED.
payload.expected_next_step: Reopen only if evidence appears for live CPU-topology change without StartTimestamp change, or for a production-feasible TiFlash same-second restart with address reuse and observable stale stream_count impact.
payload.stop_rule: Do not execute a RED test on token equality alone; do not count this as a bug without G3 product-schedule proof and a stronger effect oracle.

provenance.source: manual target-analysis after store.py source-targets identity-token
